references.text: Jesus speaks about the one who harvests receiving a wage (μισθὸν λαμβάνει). This connects to the principle of the worker's wage, also mentioned in Luke 10:7 where Jesus says that "the worker is worthy of his wages".
In Daniel 12:3 it is written that those who lead many to righteousness shall shine like the stars – a parallel to the eternal reward for the one who gathers fruit for eternal life.
Proverbs 11:30 says that "the fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who wins souls is wise". This touches on the same image of harvesting fruit that leads to life.
The immediate context in John 4:37-38 elaborates on the relationship between the one who sows and the one who harvests, showing that they have different roles but share in the joy.

In 1 Corinthians 3:6-8 Paul writes that one plants, another waters, but God gives the growth – and that each will receive their own wage according to their labor. This reflects Jesus' words that the one who sows and the one who harvests rejoice together.
The expression "fruit for eternal life" (καρπὸν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον) has a close parallel in John 6:27, where Jesus encourages working for the food that endures to eternal life.

Psalm 126:5-6 describes how the one who sows with tears shall reap with joy – an image that sowing and harvesting end in shared joy, as Jesus says the one who sows and the one who harvests rejoice together.

In Amos 9:13 it is prophesied about a time when "the plowman shall overtake the reaper", an eschatological image of abundance where sowing and harvesting meet – parallel to Jesus' words that the one who sows and the one who harvests rejoice at the same time.

Galatians 6:8-9 speaks about sowing in the Spirit and reaping eternal life, and not growing weary in doing good, for "we shall reap in due season". The parallel to gathering fruit for eternal life is clear.
In Matthew 9:37-38 Jesus speaks that the harvest is plentiful but the workers are few, and encourages praying for workers for the harvest – the same image of spiritual harvest as in John 4:36.
